arxiv-2105-15064.description: Abstract . Algorithmic Bias can be due to bias in the training data or issues with the algorithm itself. These algorithmic issues typically relate to problems with model capacity and regularisation. This underestimation bias may arise because the model has been optimized for good generalisation accuracy without any explicit consideration of bias or fairness.

Dwarf galaxies are excellent systems to investigate the dark matter density distribution, as they tend to have larger fractions of dark matter compared to higher mass systems.

arxiv-2305-17796.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Alexander Koldobsky, Michael Roysdon and Artem Zvavitch. Given two non-negative functions f f and g g such that the Radon transform of f f is pointwise smaller than the Radon transform of g g , does it follow that the L p L^{p} -norm of f f is smaller than the L p L^{p} -norm of g g for a given p > 0 ​ ? We consider this problem for the classical and spherical Radon transforms.

arxiv-2402-15989.title: PIDformer: Transformer Meets Control Theory
arxiv-2402-15989.creator: Tam Nguyen, César A. Uribe, Tan M. Nguyen, Richard G. Baraniuk
arxiv-2402-15989.description: Abstract In this work, we address two main shortcomings of transformer architectures: input corruption and rank collapse in their output representation. We unveil self-attention as an autonomous state-space model that inherently promotes smoothness in its solutions, leading to lower-rank outputs and diminished representation capacity. Moreover, the steady-state solution of the model is sensitive to input perturbations.

arxiv-2501-18539.title: Can we Retrieve Everything All at Once? ARM: An A lignment-Oriented LLM-based R etrieval M ethod
arxiv-2501-18539.creator: Peter Baile Chen, Yi Zhang, Michael Cafarella, Dan Roth
arxiv-2501-18539.description: Abstract Real-world open-domain questions can be complicated, particularly when answering them involves information from multiple information sources. LLMs have demonstrated impressive performance in decomposing complex tasks into simpler steps, and previous work has used it for better retrieval in support of complex questions.

arxiv-2506-12440.title: Style-based Composer Identification and Attribution of Symbolic Music Scores: a Systematic Survey
arxiv-2506-12440.creator: Federico Simonetta
arxiv-2506-12440.description: Abstract This paper presents the first comprehensive systematic review of literature on style-based composer identification and authorship attribution in symbolic music scores. Addressing the critical need for improved reliability and reproducibility in this field, the review rigorously analyzes 58 peer-reviewed papers published across various historical periods, with the search adapted to evolving terminology.

arxiv-2507-22437.title: On the growth of hypergeometric sequences
arxiv-2507-22437.creator: George Kenison, Jakub Konieczny, Florian Luca, Andrew Scoones, Mahsa Shirmohammadi, James Worrell
arxiv-2507-22437.description: Abstract Hypergeometric sequences obey first-order linear recurrence relations with polynomial coefficients and are commonplace throughout the mathematical and computational sciences. For certain classes of hypergeometric sequences, we prove linear growth estimates on their Weil heights. We give an application of our effective results, towards the Membership Problem from Computer Science.

arxiv-2509-16689.title: On the accuracy of twirled approximations in repeater chains
arxiv-2509-16689.creator: Bethany Davies, Guus Avis, Stephanie Wehner
arxiv-2509-16689.description: Abstract In the performance analysis of quantum networks, it is common to approximate bipartite entangled states as either being Bell-diagonal or Werner states. We refer to these as twirled approximations because it is possible to bring any state to such a form with a twirling map.

arxiv-2512-12641.title: Which Pieces Does Unigram Tokenization Really Need?
arxiv-2512-12641.creator: Sander Land, Yuval Pinter
arxiv-2512-12641.description: Abstract The Unigram tokenization algorithm offers a probabilistic alternative to the greedy heuristics of Byte-Pair Encoding. Despite its theoretical elegance, its implementation in practice is complex, limiting its adoption to the SentencePiece package and adapters thereof. We bridge this gap between theory and practice by providing a clear guide to implementation and parameter choices.

pmc-12473769.title: Machine Learning for Multi-Target Drug Discovery: Challenges and Opportunities in Systems Pharmacology
pmc-12473769.creator: Xueyuan Bi, Yangyang Wang, Jihan Wang, Cuicui Liu, Seong Hoon Jeong, Anca Zanfirescu, Corina Andrei
pmc-12473769.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Multi-target drug discovery has become an essential strategy for treating complex diseases involving multiple molecular pathways. Traditional single-target approaches often fall short in addressing the multifactorial nature of conditions such as cancer and neurodegenerative disorders. With the rise in large-scale biological data and algorithmic advances, machine learning (ML) has emerged as a powerful tool to accelerate and optimize multi-target drug development.

The three primary epidemiological cycles that contribute to the spread of ASF include ticks, wild boars, and domestic pigs.

pmc-12764650.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background and objectiveTargeting the interleukin-23 (IL-23) pathway is an emerging therapeutic strategy for moderate to severe ulcerative colitis (UC). This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of IL-23 inhibitors for induction and maintenance therapy in UC.MethodsA systematic search of PubMed, Cochrane, and Google Scholar was conducted up to May 2025 to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of IL-23 inhibitors (mirikizumab, risankizumab, guselkumab) in UC.

Thus, it is necessary to determine the subcellular localizations of circRNAs.

pmc-13434772.creator: Bijeesh Meethale Mangalassery, Simon Fabiunke, Malte Schmick, Jan Huebinger
